corrections.form_value: No outcome or robustness variant records the CLIP semantic-clustering analysis in Appendix D.3.
corrections.source_says: Include the additional semantic-diversity result from the same corpus: CLIP clip-vit-base-p32 prompt embeddings clustered at cosine similarity 0.8 with minimum cluster size 20. Consistent repeaters have 36,450 clustered prompts in 79 groups, including a cluster of 15,192 prompts; occasional repeaters have 31,223 in 166 groups; non-repeaters have 22,802 in 237 groups. These are prompt and cluster counts, not people. The initial per-category sample size is not stated here. This analysis can be recorded as a semantic-diversity variant; it is not a randomized people experiment.
corrections.quote:
Occasional
repeaters had 31,223 prompts clustered into 166 groups, while
non-repeaters, with 22,802 clustered prompts and 237 groups,
exhibited the highest number of distinct clusters and the great-
est semantic diversity.
corrections.locator: p. 27, Appendix D.3, methods and final paragraph; Figures 13-15

corrections.form_value: Section 7.2 text gives token-image r = 0.33 with R2 0.182 and text-image r = 0.43 with R2 0.109, but Figure 8 and Appendix E.1 assign R2 = 0.109 to the identical-token count and R2 = 0.1821 to token similarity.
corrections.source_says: Figure 8a prints R² = 0.109 for Number of Identical Tokens, whereas Figure 8b prints R² = 0.182 for Mean Text Embedding Similarity. Figure 8b therefore concerns semantic text-embedding similarity, and does not print 0.1821. Appendix E.1 separately labels its R² = 0.1821 analysis Token Similarity. Preserve the distinction and the source inconsistency instead of saying Figure 8 and Appendix E.1 both assign 0.1821 to token similarity.
corrections.locator: p. 11, Figure 8a-b, printed axes and R-squared labels; p. 27, Appendix E.1; compare p. 10, Section 7.2

The raw topic count increases overall, while the topics-to-prompts ratio decreases. Appendix D.1 lists 71 topics in October 2023 and 83 in April 2024; the main-text counts differ, as the form already notes, but likewise describe an overall increase rather than a uniform decrease in topic count.

semantic topics grew only modestly—rising from 72 in October

Remove each or flag the per-category denominator as unclear. corrections.form_value: Corpus: Civiverse dataset, over 6.5 million images created by 52,905 unique contributors on CivitAI, October 2023 to April 2024. After removing non-English prompts (3 percent) and 8,000 identical images with matching timestamps, 5,864,047 prompts with duplicates and 2,747,380 unique prompts; analyses use the unique-prompt subset. Users are grouped as consistent repeaters (25,058), non-repeaters (20,756), and occasional repeaters (7,091) (Table 2).
corrections.source_says: The recorded user counts match Section 3 and Table 2, but the appendix supplies conflicting category counts that should also be flagged: Table 9 lists 25,449 consistent repeaters, 7,093 occasional repeaters, and 21,835 non-repeaters, versus Table 2’s 25,058, 7,091, and 20,756. The paper does not reconcile them. Retain 52,905 as the reported corpus contributor count, and do not promote it to a verified post-exclusion people count for every sampled analysis; retaining null for an unconfirmed analysis-specific people count is appropriate.
corrections.locator: p. 3, Section 3; p. 4, Table 2; pp. 14-15, Appendix B and Table 9

corrections.source_says: Replace the empty randomized value with no and the empty preregistered value with not_stated. The paper analyzes an existing prompt-image corpus; its computational experiments cluster prompts and compare their generated images. No assignment of people to AI assistance and no preregistration are reported.
corrections.quote:
All subsequent anal-
yses in this paper rely on the unique-prompt subset, whereas
the duplicate-inclusive subset is used exclusively to classify
different user repetition behaviors.
corrections.locator: p. 3, Section 3; pp. 10-11, Section 7.2; p. 27, Appendices D.3 and E.1

corrections.form_value: Observational corpus study of CivitAI text-to-image prompts and images over seven months; no one is assigned to AI, and every output is AI-generated, so there is no with-AI versus without-AI comparison. Diversity of prompts and images is compared across months and across self-defined user groups.
corrections.source_says: Replace self-defined user groups with researcher-defined groups based on observed prompt-repetition histories. The authors classify users from their submission behavior; users are not reported to choose or declare their group. The observational context class and exclusion from the randomized core remain correct.
corrections.quote:
Additionally, categorized users into three distinct groups
based on their level of linguistic experimentation and pat-
terns in prompt submission throughout the overall dataset.

confirmed: The full markdown, appendices included, and PDF text for all 29 pages were read; Figures 3, 4, 6, and 8 were also visually inspected. The file is arXiv:2504.14125v1 [cs.HC], 19 Apr 2025, with the title and two authors recorded in the form (p. 1); appendices occupy pp. 14-29. The FAccT version of record was not read.

Design and context are observational, with no randomized people study and no unassisted comparison group. The experiments in Section 7.2 and Appendix D.3 are analyses of existing prompt/image clusters; Figures 16-17 are model-output illustrations (pp. 3-4, 10-11, 27-29). This is not a small randomized experiment with fewer than 50 people.

Section 3 reports over 6.5 million images, 52,905 unique contributors, October 2023 to April 2024, exclusion of 3% non-English prompts, removal of 8,000 identical images, and subsets of 5,864,047 prompts with duplicates and 2,747,380 unique prompts (p. 3). These distinguish corpus contributors from prompts and images; no randomized participant count is reported.
Table 2 prints 25,058 consistent repeaters, 20,756 non-repeaters, and 7,091 occasional repeaters (p. 4). These match the form, subject to the additional Table 9 inconsistency identified above.

The fixed monthly lexical sample is 213,779 prompts and the controlled lexical comparison uses 90,521 prompts per user category (p. 5, Sections 5.1 and 5.3). Vendi analysis uses 10,000 prompts with their corresponding images per category per month, 30,000 monthly samples in total (p. 9, Section 7.1); these are not people counts.

S1-O1 reproduces the printed main-text values: April TTR 0.017 full and 0.023 sampled, ENW around 3,500–3,600 in early 2024 to below 2,000 by April, SRS/CR r = −0.55, and full/sample SRS correlation 0.9956 (p. 5, Section 5.2). Figure 3 disagrees with the April TTR/ENW text; the discrepancy is real, but exact figure endpoints are not printed (p. 6).
All S1-O2 Table 4 values match: consistent repeaters TTR 0.065, ENW 2909, CR 0.26, SRS 5.75; occasional repeaters 0.076, 3483, 0.29, 5.83; non-repeaters 0.10, 3719, 0.39, 4.43 (p. 6, Table 4).

S1-O3 correctly transcribes 1,670,103 above-threshold prompts and 34,034 users versus 829,897 below-threshold prompts and 43,587 users. The text prints approximately 2.5 million sampled prompts and 66.8% above 0.8; it also specifies truncation to 20 tokens and at least 16 shared tokens (p. 7, Section 5.4 and Table 5). The two user columns are not disjoint participant arms.

The S1-O3 quoted monthly percentages 68–73%, 72.27%, 77.03%, and above 83% are printed in Section 5.4 (p. 7). The form correctly warns that the corresponding Appendix C.6/Table 28 figures describe consistent-repeaters’ share within the above-threshold group, not the overall near-duplicate rate (pp. 19-20).

S1-O4 faithfully quotes the main text’s topic counts 72 in October, 83 in December, and 89 by February and its declining topics-to-prompts ratio (p. 8, Section 6.2). The noted appendix counts are also correct: 71 October, 73 December, 81 February, 76 March, 83 April (pp. 21-25, Appendix D.1). User-category topic counts 89, 71, and 76 are printed on p. 9, Section 6.3.

S1-O5’s reported post-February Vendi decline is stated in Section 7.1 and displayed in Figure 6 (p. 9). Every Table 7 correlation/p-value pair matches: TTR 0.184/0.349, ENW 0.521/0.005, SRS -0.536/0.003, CR 0.620/0.012 (p. 10). The authors explicitly call these Pearson correlations despite using rho notation.

The one-line finding’s numerical claims match the cited main text and Table 5/Table 7 (pp. 3, 5, 7, 9-10). Its April lexical values are the internally inconsistent text claims, not reconciled estimates from Figure 3; the existing conflict caveat must be retained.

No synthesis, pooled estimate, confidence interval for a pooled estimate, or pooled standardizer is reported; the synthesis defaults are appropriate. Funding is attributed to SNSF rather than a company (p. 12, Acknowledgements).
summary: The observational classification and quoted main-text numbers are supported, with no randomized people study. Corrections address omitted appendix results, ambiguous counts, figure interpretation, outcome direction, and several form fields.
